Catena.quote: Catena, catenae CA Chain of craters

Cavus.quote: Cavus, cavi CB Hollows, irregular steep-sided depressions usually in arrays or clusters

Chaos.quote: Chaos, chaoses CH Distinctive area of broken terrain

Chasma.quote: Chasma, chasmata CM A deep, elongated, steep-sided depression

Collis.quote: Collis, colles CO Small hills or knobs

Corona.quote: Corona, coronae CR Ovoid-shaped feature Crater, craters AA A circular depression

Dorsum.quote: Dorsum, dorsa DO Ridge Eruptive center ER Active volcanic centers on Io

Facula.quote: Facula, faculae FA Bright spot Farrum, farra FR Pancake-like structure, or a row of such structures

Fluctus.quote: Fluctus, fluctūs FL Flow terrain Flumen, flumina FM Channel on Titan that might carry liquid

Fossa.quote: Fossa, fossae FO Long, narrow depression

Labyrinthus.meaning: Complex of intersecting valleys or ridges
Labyrinthus.quote: Labyrinthus, labyrinthi LB Complex of intersecting valleys or ridges.

Lacus.quote: Lacus, lacūs LC "Lake" or small plain; on Titan, a "lake" or small, dark plain with discrete, sharp boundaries

Linea.meaning: A dark or bright elongate marking, may be curved or straight
Linea.quote: Linea, lineae LI A dark or bright elongate marking, may be curved or straight

Lingula.meaning: Extension of plateau having rounded lobate or tongue-like boundaries
Lingula.quote: Lingula, lingulae LN Extension of plateau having rounded lobate or tongue-like boundaries

Mare.quote: Mare, maria ME "Sea"; on the Moon, low albedo, relatively smooth plain, generally of large extent; on Mars, dark albedo areas of no known geological significance; on Titan, large expanses of dark materials thought to be liquid hydrocarbons

Mensa.meaning: A flat-topped prominence with cliff-like edges
Mensa.quote: Mensa, mensae MN A flat-topped prominence with cliff-like edges

Mons.quote: Mons, montes MO Mountain Oceanus, oceani OC A very large dark area on the moon

Oceanus.meaning: A very large dark area on the moon
Oceanus.quote: Oceanus, oceani OC A very large dark area on the moon

Patera.meaning: An irregular crater, or a complex one with scalloped edges
Patera.quote: Patera, paterae PE An irregular crater, or a complex one with scalloped edges

Planitia.quote: Planitia, planitiae PL Low plain Planum, plana PM Plateau or high plain

Planum.quote: Planum, plana PM Plateau or high plain

Regio.meaning: A large area marked by reflectivity or color distinctions from adjacent areas, or a broad geographic region
Regio.quote: Regio, regiones RE A large area marked by reflectivity or color distinctions from adjacent areas, or a broad geographic region

Rima.quote: Rima, rimae RI Fissure Rupes, rupēs RU Scarp

Rupes.quote: Rima, rimae RI Fissure Rupes, rupēs RU Scarp

Scopulus.quote: Scopulus, scopuli SC Lobate or irregular scarp

Serpens.meaning: Sinuous feature with segments of positive and negative relief along its length
Serpens.quote: Serpens, serpentes SE Sinuous feature with segments of positive and negative relief along its length

Sinus.quote: Sinus, sinūs SI "Bay"; small plain; on Titan, bays within seas or lakes of liquid hydrocarbons

Sulcus.quote: Sulcus, sulci SU Subparallel furrows and ridges

Terra.quote: Terra, terrae TA Extensive land mass

Tessera.quote: Tessera, tesserae TE Tile-like, polygonal terrain

Tholus.quote: Tholus, tholi TH Small domical mountain or hill

Unda.quote: Unda, undae UN Dunes Vallis, valles VA Valley

Vallis.quote: Vallis, valles VA Valley Vastitas, vastitates VS Extensive plain

Vastitas.quote: Vastitas, vastitates VS Extensive plain Virga, virgae VI A streak or stripe of color

earth.name: Grand Canyon
earth.quote: The Grand Canyon has become a geologic icon—a place where you can almost sense the invisible tectonic forces within the Earth.

earth.name: Mount Fuji
earth.quote: The 3,776-meter-high (12,388 feet) Mount Fuji Volcano, located on the island of Honshu in Japan, is one of the world’s classic examples of a stratovolcano.

earth.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
earth.quote: Mount Kilimanjaro is a dormant stratovolcano and the highest mountain in Africa.

earth.name: Uluru
earth.quote: Called Uluru, or Ayer's Rock, this giant is a monolith 348 meters (1,142 feet) high, 3.6 kilometers (2.2 miles) long, and 9.4 kilometers (5.8 miles) around.

earth.name: Challenger Deep
earth.quote: The Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Marianas Trench, plunges deeper into the Earth's interior (nearly 11,000 m) than Mount Everest, the world's tallest mountain, rises above sea level (about 8,854 m).

earth.name: Mississippi River
earth.quote: Originating from Lake Itasca in Minnesota, the Mississippi River flows approximately 3,770 kilometers (2,340 miles) through 10 states before emptying into the gulf.

earth.name: Mount Etna
earth.quote: Mount Etna is considered to be the most active volcano on the European continent.

earth.name: Mount Vesuvius
earth.quote: Mount Vesuvius , located 12 kilometers (7.5 miles) southeast of Naples, Italy, is one of the few active volcanoes on Europe’s mainland.

earth.name: Hudson Bay
earth.quote: Located in northeastern Canada, just south of the Arctic Circle, Hudson Bay is the world’s second-largest bay and spans 1,230,000 square kilometers (470,000 square miles).

earth.name: Yellowstone Caldera
earth.quote: About 631,000 years ago, a massive eruption formed what today is known as Yellowstone Caldera.

earth.name: Mount Saint Helens
earth.quote: During the 1980 eruption the upper 400 m (1,300 ft) of the summit was removed by a huge debris avalanche, leaving a 2 x 3.5 km horseshoe-shaped crater now partially filled by a lava dome and a glacier.

earth.name: Mariana Trench
earth.quote: The Mariana Trench stretches 2,500 kilometers (1,500 miles) in an arc that is edged by islands such as Guam and Saipan.

earth.name: Krakatau
earth.quote: Responsible for one of the largest and most destructive eruptions in Indonesia’s history, Krakatau still erupts frequently.

earth.name: Antarctic Peninsula
earth.quote: The ice-covered and mountainous peninsula stretches 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) into the Southern Ocean.

earth.name: Aoraki/Mount Cook
earth.quote: New Zealand's highest peak, Aoraki Mount Cook, reaches 3,724 meters (12,218 feet) above sea level.

earth.name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge
earth.quote: The rate of spreading along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge averages about 2.5 centimeters per year (cm/yr), or 25 km in a million years.

earth.name: Death Valley
earth.quote: At 86 meters (282 feet) below sea level, Death Valley, California, is one of the hottest, driest places on the planet.

earth.name: Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre
earth.quote: Modern Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre is a salt-encrusted, mostly dry and barren playa that occupies Australia's lowest natural point, which is 15 meters (49 feet) below sea level.

earth.name: Kīlauea
earth.quote: Kīlauea ranks among the world's most active volcanoes.

earth.name: Mount Pinatubo
earth.quote: The second-largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century, and by far the largest eruption to affect a densely populated area, occurred at Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines on June 15, 1991.

earth.name: Eyjafjallajökull
earth.quote: Iceland’s Eyjafjallajökull Volcano sent a plume of ash and steam across the North Atlantic in mid-April 2010, prompting authorities in the United Kingdom, Ireland, France, and Scandinavia to close airspace over their countries.

earth.name: Ross Ice Shelf
earth.quote: Spanning nearly 600 miles in length, and achieving a thickness of 3000 feet in certain areas, the Ross Ice Shelf is the largest ice shelf in the world.

earth.name: Bay of Fundy
earth.quote: Under typical conditions, high tide at the head (the most inland part) of the Bay of Fundy is as much as 17 meters (about 56 feet) higher than low tide.

earth.name: Lake Superior
earth.quote: Superior is the world’s largest freshwater lake by area (82,100 square kilometers or 31,700 square miles) and the third largest by volume.

earth.name: Shark Bay
earth.quote: Shark Bay contains the largest and richest beds of seagrasses in the world and is also home to some of the oldest lifeforms on Earth.

earth.name: K'gari
earth.quote: Spanning 180,000 hectares (440,000 acres), Fraser Island (also called K'gari) is known for its tropical rainforests, sand dunes, and inland lakes.

earth.name: Popocatépetl
earth.quote: Popocatépetl is a stratovolcano, the classic symmetrical (in this case cone-shaped) mountain with a circular crater in its summit.

earth.name: Mount Tambora
earth.quote: On April 10, 1815, the Tambora Volcano produced the largest eruption in recorded history.

earth.name: Great Salt Lake
earth.quote: Few other lakes in the United States rival the Great Salt Lake in size and significance.

earth.name: Mauna Loa
earth.quote: Mauna Loa is Earth's largest active volcano and covers just over half of the Island of Hawaiʻi.

earth.name: Chimborazo
earth.quote: Sitting nearly on top of Earth's greatest equatorial bulge, Chimborazo's peak is the farthest point on the planet's surface from the center, over 2,000 meters farther from the center of the Earth than Everest's peak.

earth.name: Mount Erebus
earth.quote: Mount Erebus is thought to be the southernmost active volcano in the world.

earth.name: Nyiragongo
earth.quote: In 1977, Nyiragongo erupted fast-moving lava that flooded twenty square kilometers in about one hour.

earth.name: Chesapeake Bay
earth.quote: The Chesapeake Bay is the largest estuary in the United States and third largest in the world.

earth.name: Teide
earth.quote: The summit of the Teide stratovolcano reaches 3,718 meters (12,198 feet) above sea level.

earth.name: Crater Lake
earth.quote: Having a maximum depth of 594 m (1,949 ft), Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the United States.

earth.name: Réservoir Manicouagan
earth.quote: Manicouagan Crater was formed 214 million years ago, near the end of the Triassic Period, when an asteroid 5 kilometers (3 miles) wide struck what is now Canada.

earth.name: Meteor Crater
earth.quote: Meteor Crater, located in northern Arizona, is one of the best preserved and easily accessible impact sites on Earth.

size.quote: Meteor Crater measures 0.75 miles (1.2 kilometers) across and about 600 feet (180 meters) deep.

earth.name: Wolfe Creek Crater
earth.quote: Almost circular, Wolfe Creek Crater (also known as Wolf Creek Crater) is considered the second largest crater in the world from which meteorite fragments have been collected.

earth.name: Puerto Rico Trench
earth.quote: The Puerto Rico Trench is a tectonic plate boundary where the North American plate slides by and descends under the Caribbean plate.

earth.name: Whakaari / White Island
earth.quote: Whakaari/White Island is the tip of a submarine stratovolcano at the northern end of the Taupo Volcanic Zone and has been active for at least 150,000 years.

earth.name: Vostok Subglacial Lake
earth.quote: The biggest known subglacial lake is Lake Vostok underneath the East Antarctic Ice Sheet, holding an estimated 5000–65 000 cubic km of water beneath 4 km of ice (the water contained in Lake Vostok is enough to fill the Grand Canyon and overflow by at least 25 %).

earth.name: Mount Rainier
earth.quote: Mount Rainier, the highest peak in the Cascade Range at 4,392m (14,410 ft), forms a dramatic backdrop to the Puget Sound region.

earth.name: Vinson Massif
earth.quote: Vinson Massif is the tallest mountain in Antarctica.

earth.name: Pingualuit Crater
earth.quote: With a diameter of 3.44 kilometers (2.14 miles), Pingualuit Crater holds a lake about 267 meters (876 feet) deep.

size.quote: With a diameter of 3.44 kilometers (2.14 miles), Pingualuit Crater holds a lake about 267 meters (876 feet) deep.

earth.name: Gosses Bluff
earth.quote: Gosses Bluff was probably formed by the impact of a large comet or meteorite about 142 million years ago.

earth.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
earth.quote: The McMurdo Dry Valleys are a row of valleys west of McMurdo Sound, Antarctica, so named because of their extremely low humidity and lack of snow and ice cover.

earth.name: Thwaites Glacier
earth.quote: Indeed, Thwaites Glacier is one of the largest contributors to global sea level rise from the West Antarctic Ice Sheet.

earth.name: Larsen Ice Shelf
earth.quote: Larsen is situated along the northeastern coast of the Antarctic Peninsula, one of the fastest-warming places on the planet.

mercury.name: Caloris Planitia
mercury.quote: Very large impact basins, including Caloris (960 miles or 1,550 kilometers in diameter) and Rachmaninoff (190 miles, or 306 kilometers in diameter), were created by asteroid impacts on the planet's surface early in the solar system's history.

mercury.name: Rachmaninoff
mercury.quote: Whereas pre-MESSENGER interpretations were that volcanism on Mercury ended early in the planet's history, MESSENGER's images of Rachmaninoff reveal that some volcanism extended well beyond that time, probably into the second half of Solar System history.

mercury.name: Borealis Planitia
mercury.quote: The vast plains surrounding Mendelssohn, called Borealis Planitia, were formed by the widespread eruption of runny lava some 3.7 billion years ago.

mercury.name: Caloris Montes
mercury.quote: The floor of the Caloris basin is filled with volcanic plains , while the Caloris Montes , a ring of mountainous peaks, are found along the basin's rim.

mercury.name: Enterprise Rupes
mercury.quote: Enterprise Rupes, about 1000 km long and with over 3 km of relief, is the largest lobate scarp on Mercury!

mercury.name: Rembrandt
mercury.quote: The number per area and size distribution of impact craters superposed on Rembrandt's rim indicates that it is one of the youngest impact basins on Mercury.

mercury.name: Beagle Rupes
mercury.quote: Beagle Rupes and other scarps on Mercury are thought to be the surface expressions of thrust faults that formed from contraction as the planet's interior cooled.

mercury.name: Pantheon Fossae
mercury.quote: The dome of the Pantheon has a series of sunken panels that radiate from a central circular opening at the top of the dome, and Mercury's Pantheon Fossae is reminiscent of this pattern.

mercury.name: Mendelssohn
mercury.quote: The Mendelssohn crater was flooded with lava after an impact originally created it.

mercury.name: Raditladi
mercury.quote: Raditladi basin is relatively young, with only a few small impact craters on the basin's floor and with well-preserved basin walls and peak-ring structure.

mercury.name: Hokusai
mercury.quote: The crater has an impressive system of rays, which extend as much as a thousand kilometers (more than 600 miles) across the planet and are the longest that have yet been identified on Mercury.

mercury.name: Prokofiev
mercury.quote: MESSENGER has found evidence that within the cold, dark, permanently shadowed regions of Prokofiev, water ice is exposed on the surface.

mercury.name: Kandinsky
mercury.quote: The floor of Kandinsky is in permanent shadow and never receives direct sunlight, keeping it very cold.

mercury.name: Apollodorus
mercury.quote: The crater Apollodorus near the center of Pantheon Fossae is 41 kilometers (25 miles) in diameter.

venus.name: Ishtar Terra
venus.quote: Its surface features - most named for both real and mythical women - include Ishtar Terra, a rocky, highland area around the size of Australia near the north pole, and an even larger, South-America-sized region called Aphrodite Terra that stretches across the equator.

venus.name: Aphrodite Terra
venus.quote: Its surface features - most named for both real and mythical women - include Ishtar Terra, a rocky, highland area around the size of Australia near the north pole, and an even larger, South-America-sized region called Aphrodite Terra that stretches across the equator.

venus.name: Ovda Regio
venus.quote: Ovda Regio is a highland region that rises over 4 kilometers (2.5 miles) above the surrounding plain.

venus.name: Niobe Planitia
venus.quote: The Niobe Planitia eruption produced about 17 square miles (45 square kilometers) of rock, which would fill 54,000 Olympic swimming pools.

venus.name: Atla Regio
venus.quote: The geological changes Herrick found occurred in Atla Regio, a vast highland region near Venus' equator that hosts two of the planet's largest volcanoes, Ozza Mons and Maat Mons.

venus.name: Artemis Corona
venus.quote: Its circular shape and size (2100 km or 1302 miles in diameter) make Artemis the largest corona identified to date on the surface of Venus.

venus.name: Lakshmi Planum
venus.quote: Lakshmi Planum is an elevated plateau plain that is bounded on all sides by mountain chains.

venus.name: Alpha Regio
venus.quote: In 1963 Alpha Regio was the first feature on Venus to be identified from Earth based radar.

venus.name: Maxwell Montes
venus.quote: The Maxwell Montes are the highest mountains on Venus, rising up to 11 km above the mean planetary surface.

venus.name: Maat Mons
venus.quote: A new study found one of Maat Mons' vents became enlarged and changed shape over an eight-month period in 1991, indicating an eruptive event occurred.

venus.name: Gula Mons
venus.quote: Gula Mons, a 3 kilometer (1.9 mile) high volcano, is located at approximately 22 degrees north latitude, 359 degrees east longitude in western Eistla Regio.

venus.name: Mead
venus.quote: At 280 km diameter, Mead is the largest impact crater on Venus.

venus.name: Sacajawea Patera
venus.quote: The formation of Sacajawea is thought to be related to the drainage and collapse of a large magma chamber.

venus.name: Sapas Mons
venus.quote: Sapas Mons, a volcano 400 kilometers (248 miles) across and 1.5 kilometers (0.9 mile) high is located at approximately 8 degrees north latitude, 188 degrees east longitude, on the western edge of Atla Regio.

venus.name: Cleopatra
venus.quote: Cleopatra is a double-ring impact basin about 100 kilometers (62 miles) in diameter and 2.5 kilometers (1.5 miles) deep.

moon.name: Tycho
moon.quote: Tycho crater is an one of the most prominent craters on the Moon -- it appears as a bright spot in the southern highlands with rays of bright material that stretch across much of the nearside.

moon.name: Clavius
moon.quote: One of the oldest and largest craters on the Moon's near side, 225 kilometer diameter Clavius is due south (above) of Tycho.

moon.name: Oceanus Procellarum
moon.quote: Oceanus Procellarum, or the Ocean of Storms, is the largest of the dark maria visible to the naked eye on the near side of the Moon.

moon.name: Mare Imbrium
moon.quote: Mare Imbrium is the second largest basin on the visible side of the Moon, with a diameter of 1250 km, and is one of the youngest of the lunar maria (the youngest is Mare Orientale) at between 3700 and 3900 million years old.

moon.name: Mare Tranquillitatis
moon.quote: The Seas of Tranquility and Serenity are calm today. They're calm most every day though, since they are actually lunar maria , ancient lava flows filling in large impact basins on the Moon

moon.name: Mare Serenitatis
moon.quote: Mare Serenitatis is one of the lunar maria, that are vast lava plains on the lunar surface. It formed between 3.9 and 3.8 thousand million years ago, a period in which the Moon was heavily bombarded by asteroids and the major impact basins on the Moon were formed.

moon.name: Mare Crisium
moon.quote: Mare Crisium is a large, dark, basaltic plain on the Moon that filled an ancient asteroid impact.

moon.name: Mare Humorum
moon.quote: Mare Humorum, or 'Sea of Moisture', is a small circular mare on the lunar nearside, about 825 kilometres across.

moon.name: Mare Orientale
moon.quote: Shaped like a target ring bull's-eye, the Mare Orientale is one of the most striking large scale lunar features.

moon.name: Vallis Schroteri
moon.quote: It includes the densest concentration of lunar sinuous rilles, including the largest known, Vallis Schroteri, which is about 160 km long, up to 11 km wide, and 1 km deep.

moon.name: Rima Hadley
moon.quote: Hadley Rille is thought to have been carved by an ancient lava flow, dating back just over 3 billion years to soon after the Moon formed.

moon.name: Plato
moon.quote: A dark floor makes 63-mile-wide (101-kilometer-wide) Plato crater stand out against a light-colored lunar highlands background.

moon.name: Copernicus
moon.quote: Copernicus is 93 km wide and is located within the Mare Imbrium Basin, northern nearside of the Moon (10 degrees N. 20 degrees W.).

moon.name: Aristarchus
moon.quote: Aristarchus Crater is the largest impact on the plateau and is one of the highest reflectance (blindingly bright in a telescope) features on the moon.

moon.name: Taurus Littrow Valley
moon.quote: The Lunar Module Challenger landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley on December 11, 1972 and remained there for 75 hours. The landing site is a relatively flat spot among low mountains at the southeastern edge of Mare Serenitatis.

moon.name: Shackleton
moon.quote: Because of its location, most of Shackleton's interior lies in permanent shadow.

mars.name: Valles Marineris
mars.quote: A vast canyon system called Valles Marineris is long enough to stretch from California to New York

mars.name: Olympus Mons
mars.quote: Olympus Mons stands more than 25 miles (that's more than 132,000 feet, or 40 kilometers) tall from base to summit, with the base covering an area as large as the state of Arizona.

mars.name: Elysium Planitia
mars.quote: Just north of the divide lies the Central Elysium Planitia -one of two large volcanic regions on Mars and the location of the youngest volcanic rocks (about two million years old) on the planet.

mars.name: Hellas Planitia
mars.quote: Hellas is an ancient impact structure and is the deepest and broadest enclosed basin on Mars. It measures about 2,300 kilometers across and the floor of the basin, Hellas Planitia, contains the lowest elevations on Mars.

mars.name: Tharsis Montes
mars.quote: Each Tharsis Montes volcano is 350-400 km in diameter and about 17 km above the surrounding plain.

mars.name: Ares Vallis
mars.quote: The Ares Vallis region of Mars is a large outwash plain near Chryse Planitia.

mars.name: Cerberus Fossae
mars.quote: One surprise is that all of InSight's most significant quakes appear to have come from one area, Cerberus Fossae , a region volcanically active enough that lava may have flowed there within the last few million years.

mars.name: Syrtis Major Planum
mars.quote: Syrtis Major is one of the darkest regions on Mars and it is as dark as fresh basalt flows or dunes are on Earth.

mars.name: Noctis Labyrinthus
mars.quote: Noctis Labyrinthus is notable for its unusual pattern of intersecting valleys, which give the region a maze-like appearance when viewed from above.

mars.name: Meridiani Planum
mars.quote: Opportunity landed at Meridiani Planum, a place where mineral deposits suggested that Mars had a wet history.

mars.name: Arsia Mons
mars.quote: The southernmost of the three Tharsis volcanoes, Arsia Mons is 270 miles (450 kilometers) in diameter and almost 12 miles (20 kilometers) high.

mars.name: Elysium Mons
mars.quote: Elysium Mons, whose summit elevation is 16,000 m above the Martian datum, is at the crest of a regional topographic rise that emerges steeply and abruptly from the surrounding plains.

mars.name: Planum Boreum
mars.quote: The terrain surrounding Mars's north pole, known as Planum Boreum , is fascinating. The pole itself is covered in layers and layers of fine dust and water ice; these stack several kilometres thick and stretch out for around 1000 km (approximately the width of France).

mars.name: Gusev
mars.quote: Gusev Crater was chosen as a landing site because it has the appearance of a crater lakebed.

mars.name: Gale
mars.quote: The landing site in Gale Crater was chosen for its potential as a former or current habitat for life.

mars.name: Aeolis Mons
mars.quote: Mount Sharp, also called Aeolis Mons, is a layered mound in the center of Mars' Gale Crater, rising more than 3 miles (5 kilometers) above the crater floor, where Curiosity has been working since the rover's landing in August 2012.

mars.name: Jezero
mars.quote: Jezero Crater tells a story of the on-again, off-again nature of the wet past of Mars.
